evals.prompt: Join ./outputs/a.mp4 and ./outputs/b.mp4. FFmpeg is not installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/check_ffmpeg.py --json, sees ok false, shows install_command, and waits. Does not download a binary or pipe a script into a shell. Does not run ffmpeg.
assertions: Ran python3 scripts/check_ffmpeg.py --json before any ffmpeg command
Showed install_command to the user and waited for confirmation
Did not run the install command before the user agreed
Did not download an FFmpeg binary or pipe a remote script into a shell
Did not call modellix-cli or a Modellix generation API

evals.prompt: Concatenate ./outputs/wide.mp4 (1920x1080, 30fps) and ./outputs/tall.mp4 (1080x1920, 24fps) into ./outputs/joined.mp4. FFmpeg is already installed.
evals.expected_output: Probes both files, refuses stream copy because resolution and frame rate differ, then re-encodes to a shared frame and concatenates. Does not overwrite either input.
assertions: Probed both inputs with ffprobe before choosing copy or re-encode
Re-encoded both clips to one shared width, height, and frame rate
Wrote ./outputs/joined.mp4 and did not overwrite wide.mp4 or tall.mp4
Did not call modellix-cli or a Modellix generation API

evals.prompt: Generate a new five-second video of a fox walking through snow. I do not have any local clips.
evals.expected_output: Hands the request to modellix-design. Does not invent an FFmpeg command for a prompt, and does not submit a Modellix task from this skill.
assertions: Did not run ffmpeg for a prompt that has no local media
Did not submit, poll, or download a Modellix task from modellix-ffmpeg

evals.prompt: Trim the first three seconds of ./outputs/scene.mp4. FFmpeg is installed. Put the result next to the source.
evals.expected_output: Asks for an output path if none was given, or writes a new file. Uses re-encode rather than stream copy. Does not delete or overwrite scene.mp4.
assertions: Asked for an output path or wrote a different new file
Re-encoded the trim instead of using -c copy
Passed -n unless the user had already asked to replace that output file
